np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(t.NdroppedFrames)).ravel()\n        return ts, ft, (nd[0] if nd.size else np.nan)\n\n    def ntraj_trials(self, view=0):\n        if self.hdf5:\n            return self.f[self.obj['traj'][()][view, 0]]['ts'].shape[0]\n        return len(self.obj.traj[view])\n\n    def vidshift(self):\n        \"\"\"funcs/findVideoOffset.m: mode(sglx.bitcode.bitstart)/fs - mode(bp.ev.bitStart)\"\"\"\n        from scipy.stats import mode as _mode\n        bitStart = _mode(self.ev('bitStart'), keepdims=False).mode\n        if self.hdf5:\n            bs = np.asarray(self.obj['sglx/bitcode/bitstart'][()]).ravel()\n            fs = float(np.asarray(self.obj['sglx/fs'][()]).ravel()[0])\n        else:\n            bs = np.atleast_1d(np.asarray(self.obj.sglx.bitcode.bitstart, dtype=float)).ravel()\n            fs = float(np.asarray(self.obj.sglx.fs).ravel()[0])\n        bs = bs[~np.isnan(bs)]\n        return float(_mode(bs, keepdims=False).mode / fs - bitStart)\n\n    def probe_locs(self):\n        out = []\n        try:\n            if self.hdf5:\n                d = self.obj['ex/probe/loc']\n                if d.dtype == object:\n                    pl = d[()]\n                    out = [_h5str(self.f, pl[i, 0]).strip() for i in range(pl.shape[0])]\n                else:\n                    out = [''.join(chr(int(c)) for c in np.asarray(d[()]).ravel()).strip()]\n            else:\n                loc = self.obj.ex.probe.loc\n                out = [str(x).strip() for x in np.atleast_1d(loc)]\n        except Exception:\n            pass\n        return out\n\n    def close(self):\n        if self.hdf5:\n            self.f.close()\n\n\ndef load_motion_energy(fn):\n    \"\"\"Return (list of per-trial motion-energy arrays, moveThresh or None).\n\n    Three file variants exist in the dataset: me struct with cell .data, me struct\n    whose .data is itself a struct (JEB15), and a bare cell array (some JEB23).\n    \"\"\"\n    me = sio.loadmat(fn)['me']\n    thresh = [None]\n\n    def unpack(x):\n        if isinstance(x, np.ndarray) and x.dtype.names is not None and 'data' in x.dtype.names:\n            if 'moveThresh' in x.dtype.names:\n                t = x['moveThresh']\n                t = t[0, 0] if t.dtype == object else t\n                t = np.asarray(t).ravel()\n                if t.size:\n                    thresh[0] = float(t[0])\n            d = x['data']\n            d = d[0, 0] if d.dtype == object and d.shape == (1, 1) else d\n            return unpack(d)\n        return x\n\n    data = np.asarray(unpack(me))\n    if data.dtype == object:\n        trials = [np.asarray(data.ravel()[i], dtype=float).ravel() for i in range(data.size)]\n    else:\n        trials = [np.asarray(data, dtype=float).ravel()]\n    return trials, thresh[0]\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Signal processing helpers (ports of utils/mySmooth.m and DataLoadingScripts/getSeq.m)\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef time_axis():\n    \"\"\"getSeq.m: edges = tmin:dt:tmax; time = edges + dt/2 with the last dropped.\"\"\"\n    nedges = int(np.floor((TMAX - TMIN) / DT)) + 1\n    edges = TMIN + DT * np.arange(nedges)\n    t = edges + DT / 2.0\n    return edges, t[:-1]\n\n\ndef gausswin(N, alpha=2.5):\n    \"\"\"MATLAB gausswin(N, alpha).\"\"\"\n    n = np.arange(N) - (N - 1) / 2.0\n    return np.exp(-0.5 * (alpha * n / ((N - 1) / 2.0)) ** 2)\n\n\ndef causal_kernel(N=SMOOTH):\n    \"\"\"mySmooth.m kernel: gausswin with the first half zeroed (causal), normalized.\"\"\"\n    k = gausswin(N)\n    k[:N // 2] = 0.0\n    return k / k.sum()\n\n\ndef mysmooth(x, N=SMOOTH, bctype='reflect'):\n    \"\"\"Port of utils/mySmooth.m; smooths along axis 0.\"\"\"\n    if N <= 1:\n        return x\n    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)\n    if bctype == 'reflect':\n        xf = np.concatenate([x[:N], x], axis=0)\n        trim = N\n    elif bctype == 'zeropad':\n        xf = np.concatenate([np.zeros((N,) + x.shape[1:]), x], axis=0)\n        trim = N\n    else:\n        xf, trim = x, 0\n    k = causal_kernel(N)\n    from scipy.signal import fftconvolve\n    if xf.ndim == 1:\n        out = fftconvolve(xf, k, mode='same')\n    else:\n        out = fftconvolve(xf, k.reshape((-1,) + (1,) * (xf.ndim - 1)), mode='same', axes=0)\n    return out[trim:]\n\n\ndef bin_spikes(clusters, gocue, ntrials, edges):\n    \"\"\"alignSpikes.m + getSeq.m: aligned spike counts -> smoothed rates.\n\n    Returns\n        rates: (ntrials, nbins, nunits) smoothed firing rates in spikes/s\n        meanfr: (nunits,) mean firing rate over the whole window and all trials,\n                computed from the raw (unsmoothed) counts. This is the quantity\n                thresholded by removeLowFRClusters.m (whose first PSTH condition,\n                '(hit|miss|no)', covers every trial) and by the paper's\n                \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\" criterion.\n    \"\"\"\n    nbins = len(edges) - 1\n    rates = np.zeros((ntrials, nbins, len(clusters)), dtype=np.float32)\n    meanfr = np.zeros(len(clusters))\n    trial_edges = np.arange(0.5, ntrials + 1.5, 1.0)  # trial numbers are 1-based\n    window = edges[-1] - edges[0]\n    for i, c in enumerate(clusters):\n        tr = np.asarray(c['trial'], dtype=float).ravel()\n        tt = np.asarray(c['trialtm'], dtype=float).ravel()\n        n = min(tr.size, tt.size)\n        tr, tt = tr[:n], tt[:n]\n        ok = (tr >= 1) & (tr <= ntrials) & np.isfinite(tt)\n        tr, tt = tr[ok], tt[ok]\n        aligned = tt - gocue[(tr - 1).astype(int)]     # trialtm_aligned\n        cnt, _, _ = np.histogram2d(tr, aligned, bins=[trial_edges, edges])\n        meanfr[i] = cnt.sum() / (ntrials * window)\n        rates[:, :, i] = mysmooth(cnt.T / DT).T.astype(np.float32)\n    return rates, meanfr\n\n\ndef interp_to_axis(src_t, src_y, taxis):\n    \"\"\"Linear interpolation like MATLAB interp1 (NaN outside the source range).\"\"\"\n    src_t = np.asarray(src_t, dtype=float)\n    src_y = np.asarray(src_y, dtype=float)\n    good = np.isfinite(src_t)\n    if good.sum() < 2:\n        return np.full((taxis.size,) + src_y.shape[1:], np.nan)\n    st = src_t[good]\n    sy = src_y[good]\n    order = np.argsort(st)\n    st, sy = st[order], sy[order]\n    inside = (taxis >= st[0]) & (taxis <= st[-1])\n    if sy.ndim == 1:\n        out = np.full(taxis.size, np.nan)\n        out[inside] = np.interp(taxis[inside], st, sy)\n    else:\n        out = np.full((taxis.size, sy.shape[1]), np.nan)\n        for j in range(sy.shape[1]):\n            out[inside, j] = np.interp(taxis[inside], st, sy[:, j])\n    return out\n\n\ndef speed_from_xy(xy):\n    \"\"\"Speed of a DLC feature, computed like findVelocity.m (gradient of position),\n    but evaluated separately within each contiguous run of frames in which the\n    feature is visible.\n\n    The reference code fills the tongue's missing frames with a baseline position\n    and sets its velocity to 0 where it is not visible. Here 'not visible' is its\n    own output class, so the velocity is left undefined (NaN) on those frames and\n    computed from neighbouring visible frames only; np.gradient uses one-sided\n    differences at the ends of each run, so every visible frame gets a value and\n    no NaN leaks into visible frames.\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = np.isfinite(xy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(xy[:, 1])\n    spd = np.full(xy.shape[0], np.nan)\n    if not vis.any():\n        return spd\n    idx = np.flatnonzero(vis)\n    breaks = np.flatnonzero(np.diff(idx) > 1)\n    starts = np.concatenate([[0], breaks + 1])\n    stops = np.concatenate([breaks, [idx.size - 1]])\n    for a, b in zip(starts, stops):\n        seg = idx[a:b + 1]\n        if seg.size == 1:\n            spd[seg] = 0.0                      # single visible frame: no motion estimate\n            continue\n        vx = np.gradient(xy[seg, 0])\n        vy = np.gradient(xy[seg, 1])\n        spd[seg] = np.sqrt(vx ** 2 + vy ** 2)\n    return spd\n\n\ndef discretize(values, visible, thresh):\n    \"\"\"0 = below threshold, 1 = at/above threshold, 2 = not visible / no video.\"\"\"\n    out = np.full(values.shape, 2, dtype=np.int64)\n    v = visible & np.isfinite(values)\n    out[v & (values < thresh)] = 0\n    out[v & (values >= thresh)] = 1\n    return out\n\n\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Per-session conversion\n# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------\ndef region_from_loc(loc):\n    \"\"\"Map obj.ex.probe.loc strings to a brain-region name.\"\"\"\n    u = (loc or '').upper()\n    if 'M1TJ' in u or 'TJM1' in u:\n        return 'tjM1'\n    return 'ALM'        # '', 'DUMMY', 'R ALM', 'L ALM' -> ALM (all reference probes are ALM recordings)\n\n\ndef process_session(entry, want_debug=False):\n    \"\"\"Convert one session. Returns a dict with neural/input/output and metadata.\"\"\"\n    t0 = time.time()\n    d, anm, date, probes = entry\n    sess_id = f'{anm}_{date}'\n    s = Session(data_path(entry))\n    timing = {}\n\n    edges, taxis = time_axis()\n    nbins = taxis.size\n    ntrials = s.ntrials\n    gocue = s.ev(ALIGN_EVENT)\n\n    # ---------------- trial curation (reference condition strings) -------------\n    stim = s.bpvec('stim/enable') if s.has_bp_field('stim') else np.zeros(ntrials)\n    early = s.bpvec('early')\n    hit = s.bpvec('hit')\n    miss = s.bpvec('miss')\n    no = s.bpvec('no')\n    autowater = s.bpvec('autowater')\n    for v in (stim, early, hit, miss, no, autowater):\n        v[np.isnan(v)] = 0\n    keep = (stim[:ntrials] == 0) & (early[:ntrials] == 0) & np.isfinite(gocue[:ntrials])\n    # a trial must be one of hit / miss / ignore\n    keep &= (hit[:ntrials] + miss[:ntrials] + no[:ntrials]) > 0\n    trials = np.where(keep)[0]\n\n    # ---------------- neural ---------------------------------------------------\n    t1 = time.time()\n    clusters, qualities, cl_region = [], [], []\n    for p in probes:\n        loc_list = s.probe_locs()\n        loc = loc_list[p - 1] if len(loc_list) >= p else ''\n        reg = region_from_loc(loc)\n        for c in s.clusters(p - 1):\n            q = c['quality'].strip().lower()\n            if q in BAD_QUALITY:\n                continue                      # findClusters.m with quality = 'all'\n            clusters.append(c)\n            qualities.append(q)\n            cl_region.append(reg)\n    rates, meanfr = bin_spikes(clusters, gocue, ntrials, edges)  # (ntrials, nbins, nunits)\n    timing['neural_bin'] = time.time() - t1\n\n    # removeLowFRClusters.m: mean rate must exceed lowFR (1 spk/s)\n    keep_units = meanfr > LOW_FR\n    rates = rates[:, :, keep_units]\n    cl_region = [r for r, k in zip(cl_region, keep_units) if k]\n    qualities = [q for q, k in zip(qualities, keep_units) if k]\n    nunits = rates.shape[2]\n\n    # Trials in which no curated unit fired a single spike in the whole 5 s window\n    # have no ephys coverage (in 2 JEB24 sessions the recording stopped before the\n    # behavioural session ended); drop them.\n    if nunits > 0:\n        has_spikes = rates[trials].sum(axis=(1, 2)) > 0\n        n_nospk = int((~has_spikes).sum())\n        trials = trials[has_spikes]\n    else:\n        n_nospk = 0\n\n    # ---------------- behavior (per-trial outputs) -----------------------------\n    lickL, lickR = s.ev_cell('lickL'), s.ev_cell('lickR')\n    lick_dir = np.full(ntrials, 2, dtype=np.int64)          # 2 = none\n    for i in range(ntrials):\n        tl = np.concatenate([lickL[i] - gocue[i], lickR[i] - gocue[i]])\n        side = np.concatenate([np.zeros(lickL[i].size), np.ones(lickR[i].size)])\n        m = tl > 0                                           # firstLickTime.m keeps post-go-cue licks\n        if m.any():\n            lick_dir[i] = int(side[m][np.argmin(tl[m])])     # 0 = left, 1 = right\n    context = np.where(autowater[:ntrials] > 0, 0, 1).astype(np.int64)   # 0 = WC, 1 = DR\n    outcome = np.full(ntrials, 2, dtype=np.int64)            # 2 = ignore\n    outcome[miss[:ntrials] > 0] = 0                          # 0 = incorrect\n    outcome[hit[:ntrials] > 0] = 1                           # 1 = correct\n\n    # ---------------- video-derived outputs ------------------------------------\n    t1 = time.time()\n    vidshift = s.vidshift()\n    fn0, fn1 = s.feat_names(0), s.feat_names(1)\n    i_tongue = fn0.index('tongue')\n    i_paws = [fn1.index(f) for f in ('top_paw', 'bottom_paw') if f in fn1]\n    me_trials, _ = load_motion_energy(me_path(entry))\n    nvid = min(s.ntraj_trials(0), s.ntraj_trials(1))\n\n    tongue_spd = np.full((ntrials, nbins), np.nan)\n    tongue_vis = np.zeros((ntrials, nbins), dtype=bool)\n    paw_spd = np.full((ntrials, nbins), np.nan)\n    paw_vis = np.zeros((ntrials, nbins), dtype=bool)\n    me_binned = np.full((ntrials, nbins), np.nan)\n    has_video = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=bool)\n\n    bin_edges = edges\n    for i in trials:\n        if i >= nvid:\n            continue\n        ts0, ft0, nd0 = s.traj_trial(0, i)\n        ts1, ft1, nd1 = s.traj_trial(1, i)\n        if ts0.size == 0 or ft0.size == 0 or np.all(~np.isfinite(ft0)) or not np.isfinite(nd0):\n            continue                                        # findPosition.m skips these trials\n        # video clock -> time from the alignment event\n        vt0 = ft0 - vidshift - gocue[i]\n        dtf = np.median(np.diff(ft0)) if ft0.size > 1 else 1 / 400.0\n        has_video[i] = True\n        idx = np.digitize(vt0, bin_edges) - 1               # bin index for each frame\n        inb = (idx >= 0) & (idx < nbins)\n\n        # --- tongue (side cam) ---\n        xy = ts0[:, :2, i_tongue]\n        vis = np.isfinite(xy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(xy[:, 1])\n        spd = speed_from_xy(xy) / dtf                        # pixels / s\n        _accumulate(idx, inb, spd, vis, tongue_spd, tongue_vis, i, nbins)\n\n        # --- paws (bottom cam) ---\n        if ts1.size and ft1.size and np.isfinite(nd1):\n            vt1 = ft1 - vidshift - gocue[i]\n            idx1 = np.digitize(vt1, bin_edges) - 1\n            inb1 = (idx1 >= 0) & (idx1 < nbins)\n            dtf1 = np.median(np.diff(ft1)) if ft1.size > 1 else 1 / 400.0\n            spds, viss = [], []\n            for j in i_paws:\n                pxy = ts1[:, :2, j]\n                spds.append(speed_from_xy(pxy) / dtf1)\n                viss.append(np.isfinite(pxy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(pxy[:, 1]))\n            with warnings.catch_warnings():\n                warnings.simplefilter('ignore')\n                spd_p = np.nanmean(np.vstack(spds), axis=0)\n            vis_p = np.any(np.vstack(viss), axis=0)\n            _accumulate(idx1, inb1, spd_p, vis_p, paw_spd, paw_vis, i, nbins)\n\n        # --- motion energy (loadMotionEnergy.m: interp to taxis, fill nearest) ---\n        if i < len(me_trials):\n            mev = me_trials[i]\n            n = min(mev.size, vt0.size)\n            if n > 1:\n                y = interp_to_axis(vt0[:n], mev[:n], taxis)\n                y = _fill_nearest(y)\n                me_binned[i] = y\n\n    timing['video'] = time.time() - t1\n\n    # ---------------- discretization (per-session 50th percentile) -------------\n    sel = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=bool)\n    sel[trials] = True\n    m_t = sel[:, None] & tongue_vis & np.isfinite(tongue_spd)\n    m_p = sel[:, None] & paw_vis & np.isfinite(paw_spd)\n    m_m = sel[:, None] & np.isfinite(me_binned)\n    thr_t = np.nanpercentile(tongue_spd[m_t], 50) if m_t.any() else np.nan\n    thr_p = np.nanpercentile(paw_spd[m_p], 50) if m_p.any() else np.nan\n    thr_m = np.nanpercentile(me_binned[m_m], 50) if m_m.any() else np.nan\n\n    tongue_cls = discretize(tongue_spd, tongue_vis, thr_t)\n    paw_cls = discretize(paw_spd, paw_vis, thr_p)\n    me_cls = discretize(me_binned, has_video[:, None] & np.isfinite(me_binned), thr_m)\n\n    # ---------------- assemble -------------------------------------------------\n    neural, inp, outp = [], [], []\n    tin = taxis.astype(np.float32).reshape(1, -1)\n    for i in trials:\n        neural.append(np.ascontiguousarray(rates[i].T))           # (nunits, nbins)\n        inp.append(tin.copy())\n        o = np.empty((6, nbins), dtype=np.int64)\n        o[0] = lick_dir[i]\n        o[1] = context[i]\n        o[2] = outcome[i]\n        o[3] = tongue_cls[i]\n        o[4] = paw_cls[i]\n        o[5] = me_cls[i]\n        outp.append(o)\n\n    res = dict(\n        session_id=sess_id, animal=anm, date=date, group=('fixed' if entry in FIXED else 'randomized'),\n        neural=neural, input=inp, output=outp,\n        regions=cl_region, qualities=qualities, nunits=nunits,\n        ntrials_total=ntrials, ntrials_kept=len(trials), trials=trials,\n        thresholds=dict(tongue=float(thr_t), paw=float(thr_p), me=float(thr_m)),\n        vidshift=vidshift, timing=timing, elapsed=time.time() - t0,\n        n_novideo=int(np.sum(~has_video[trials])), n_nospike=n_nospk,\n    )\n    if want_debug:\n        res['debug'] = dict(taxis=taxis, rates=rates, tongue_spd=tongue_spd, tongue_vis=tongue_vis,\n                            paw_spd=paw_spd, paw_vis=paw_vis, me=me_binned, has_video=has_video,\n                            lick_dir=lick_dir, context=context, outcome=outcome, gocue=gocue,\n                            lickL=lickL, lickR=lickR, clusters_kept=int(nunits))\n    s.close()\n    return res\n\n\ndef _accumulate(idx, inb, spd, vis, spd_out, vis_out, trial, nbins):\n    \"\"\"Average per-frame speed within each time bin; a bin is visible if any frame is.\"\"\"\n    good = inb & vis & np.isfinite(spd)\n    if good.any():\n        sums = np.bincount(idx[good], weights=spd[good], minlength=nbins)\n        cnts = np.bincount(idx[good], minlength=nbins)\n        with np.errstate(invalid='ignore', divide='ignore'):\n            vals = np.where(cnts > 0, sums / np.maximum(cnts, 1), np.nan)\n        spd_out[trial] = vals\n        vis_out[trial] = cnts > 0\n\n\ndef _fill_nearest(y):\n    \"\"\"MATLAB fillmissing(y,'nearest') for a 1-D array.\"\"\"\n    y = np.asarray(y, dtype=float).copy()\n    good = np.isfinite(y)\n    if not good.any() or good.all():\n        return y\n    gi = np.flatnonzero(good)\n    bi = np.flatnonzero(~good)\n    pos = np.searchsorted(gi, bi)\n    left = np.clip(pos - 1, 0, gi.size - 1)\n    right = np.clip(pos, 0, gi.size - 1)\n    take_left = np.abs(bi - gi[left]) <= np.abs(gi[right] - bi)\n    nearest = np.where(take_left, gi[left], gi[right])\n    y[bi] = y[nearest]\n    return y\n\n\n# In WC trials `bp.ev.goCue` holds the water-drop time, so the alignment is meaningful in both contexts.\n195\t2. **Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\n196\t3. **Causal Gaussian smoothing, N=15 bins, 'reflect'** exactly as `mySmooth` — causal so no information from the future leaks backwards in time (important for a decoder).\n197\t4. **Neuron curation**: quality not in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, empty} (findClusters, case-insensitive/trimmed to handle label case and typos) AND mean firing rate over the trial window > 1 Hz (removeLowFRClusters with `lowFR=1`, matching the paper's \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"). Sessions with < 10 units would be dropped (paper criterion); in practice all 44 pass.\n198\t5. **Probe selection**: use exactly the probe(s) listed in the reference meta scripts (`load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m`). These are the probes the paper analysed. For each kept probe the recorded region is read from `obj.ex.probe.loc` ('R ALM'/'L ALM' -> ALM, 'M1TJ' -> tjM1); when `loc` is missing or 'DUMMY', ALM is assumed (all the loader scripts are named *_ALMVideo and the paper states all recordings analysed were ALM). Consequence: for JEB15 2022-07-26/27/28 the reference uses probes [1 2] where probe 2 is 'L M1TJ', and for JEB15 2022-07-29 the reference uses probe 2 ('L M1TJ'); those neurons are labelled tjM1 so that `brain_region_idx` is truthful, rather than dropping data the reference analysed.\n199\t6. **Trial curation**: exclude photoinactivation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) and early-lick trials (`bp.early`), exactly as every reference condition string does ('~stim.enable&~early') and as stated in the methods (\"Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward ('early lick') were omitted from analyses\"). **Ignore trials are kept** because 'ignore' and 'none' are required output classes.\n200\t7. **Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class** instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`. This is required by the decoder output specification, which asks for an explicit 'not visible' category.\n201\t8. **Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\n202\t9. **Session curation**: keep a session only if it has >= 10 curated units (paper criterion) and at least 2 usable trials. No session is dropped for probe-location reasons (see Decision 5).\n203\t10. **Video/ephys synchronisation** uses `vidshift` from `findVideoOffset.m` for both DLC and motion energy, as in the reference.\n204\t\n205\t### Planned Sanity Checks\n206\t- [ ] Number of sessions = 44 (25 fixed + 19 randomized), animals = 14.\n207\t- [ ] Units after curation: randomized-delay total = 845 (matches paper exactly).\n208\t- [ ] Every session has >= 10 units; neurons/session distribution similar to ED Fig 2a (13-130).\n209\t- [ ] Trial counts: sum of kept trials ~= total trials - early - stim.\n210\t- [ ] Lick direction from first lick agrees with hit/miss x R/L in >99% of trials.\n211\t- [ ] Outcome fractions: hit ~70%, miss ~12%, ignore ~13% (from raw bp fields).\n212\t- [ ] Context fraction WC ~10-20% of trials overall (sessions with two contexts: 12 of 25 fixed-delay).\n213\t- [ ] Each discretized output has ~50/50 split between classes 0 and 1 among visible timepoints.\n214\t- [ ] Spot check (Step 10): recompute neural rate, tongue speed, ME for specific trials directly from the raw .mat files with independent code and compare with `np.allclose`.\n215\t- [ ] Time axis: bin centers from -2.485 to 2.485, dt exactly 0.03 s.\n216\t\n217\t---\n218\t\n219\t## Step 6: Script Development\n220\t**Status**: COMPLETE\n221\t\n222\t`/app/convert_data.py` is self-contained (no imports from `/app/cache`). probe 2 there is L M1TJ per `obj.ex.probe.loc`, so for those sessions we keep **only the ALM probe** -> see Key Decisions).\n- `subjects` = the 14 animals; `subject_idx` per session.\n- `brain_regions` = ['ALM']; every included neuron is in ALM.\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\n| `obj.clu{alm}.trialtm`, `.trial` | `neural` | align to go cue (subtract `bp.ev.goCue`), bin -2.5..2.5 s at dt=30 ms, rate = count/dt, causal-Gaussian smooth (N=15, 'reflect') | alignSpikes.m, getSeq.m, mySmooth.m | firing rate in spikes/s, float32 |\n| time axis | `input[0]` = `time_from_gocue` | obj.time = bin centers, seconds | getSeq.m | continuous, time-varying (1 x T) |\n| first lick after go cue (`bp.ev.lickL/lickR`) | `output[0]` = `lick_direction` | 0=left, 1=right, 2=none | firstLickTime.m | per-trial value broadcast over T |\n| `bp.autowater` | `output[1]` = `context` | 0=WC (autowater=1), 1=DR | params.condition strings | per-trial |\n| `bp.hit/miss/no` | `output[2]` = `outcome` | 0=incorrect(miss), 1=correct(hit), 2=ignore(no) | getOutcome.m | per-trial |\n| side-cam `tongue` x/y (`obj.traj{1}`) | `output[3]` = `tongue_velocity` | speed=|d(x,y)/dt| of interpolated position; 0 if < session median, 1 if >= median, 2 if tongue not visible (DLC NaN) | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m | time-varying |\n| bottom-cam `top_paw`,`bottom_paw` (`obj.traj{2}`) | `output[4]` = `paw_velocity` | mean speed of the visible paw markers; 0/1 by session median, 2 if neither paw visible | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m | time-varying |\n| `motionEnergy_*.mat` `me.data` | `output[5]` = `motion_energy` | interp to trial time axis (frameTimes - vidshift - goCue), fillmissing nearest; 0/1 by session median, 2 if the trial has no usable video | loadMotionEnergy.m | time-varying |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Alignment to go cue** (`params.alignEvent='goCue'`), window **-2.5 to +2.5 s**, exactly as in every reference analysis script. In WC trials `bp.ev.goCue` holds the water-drop time, so the alignment is meaningful in both contexts.\n2. **Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\n3. **Causal Gaussian smoothing, N=15 bins, 'reflect'** exactly as `mySmooth` — causal so no information from the future leaks backwards in time (important for a decoder).\n4. **Neuron curation**: quality not in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, empty} (findClusters, case-insensitive/trimmed to handle label case and typos) AND mean firing rate over the trial window > 1 Hz (removeLowFRClusters with `lowFR=1`, matching the paper's \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"). Sessions with < 10 units would be dropped (paper criterion); in practice all 44 pass.\n5. **Probe selection**: use exactly the probe(s) listed in the reference meta scripts (`load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m`). These are the probes the paper analysed. For each kept probe the recorded region is read from `obj.ex.probe.loc` ('R ALM'/'L ALM' -> ALM, 'M1TJ' -> tjM1); when `loc` is missing or 'DUMMY', ALM is assumed (all the loader scripts are named *_ALMVideo and the paper states all recordings analysed were ALM). Consequence: for JEB15 2022-07-26/27/28 the reference uses probes [1 2] where probe 2 is 'L M1TJ', and for JEB15 2022-07-29 the reference uses probe 2 ('L M1TJ'); those neurons are labelled tjM1 so that `brain_region_idx` is truthful, rather than dropping data the reference analysed.\n6. **Trial curation**: exclude photoinactivation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) and early-lick trials (`bp.early`), exactly as every reference condition string does ('~stim.enable&~early') and as stated in the methods (\"Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward ('early lick') were omitted from analyses\"). **Ignore trials are kept** because 'ignore' and 'none' are required output classes.\n7. **Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class** instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`. This is required by the decoder output specification, which asks for an explicit 'not visible' category.\n8. **Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\n9. **Session curation**: keep a session only if it has >= 10 curated units (paper criterion) and at least 2 usable trials. No session is dropped for probe-location reasons (see Decision 5).\n10. **Video/ephys synchronisation** uses `vidshift` from `findVideoOffset.m` for both DLC and motion energy, as in the reference.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] Number of sessions = 44 (25 fixed + 19 randomized), animals = 14.\n- [ ] Units after curation: randomized-delay total = 845 (matches paper exactly).\n- [ ] Every session has >= 10 units; neurons/session distribution similar to ED Fig 2a (13-130).\n- [ ] Trial counts: sum of kept trials ~= total trials - early - stim.\n- [ ] Lick direction from first lick agrees with hit/miss x R/L in >99% of trials.\n- [ ] Outcome fractions: hit ~70%, miss ~12%, ignore ~13% (from raw bp fields).\n- [ ] Context fraction WC ~10-20% of trials overall (sessions with two contexts: 12 of 25 fixed-delay).\n- [ ] Each discretized output has ~50/50 split between classes 0 and 1 among visible timepoints.\n- [ ] Spot check (Step 10): recompute neural rate, tongue speed, ME for specific trials directly from the raw .mat files with independent code and compare with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Time axis: bin centers from -2.485 to 2.485, dt exactly 0.03 s.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py` is self-contained (no imports from `/app/cache`). Structure:\n- `Session` class: unified reader for MAT v7 (scipy) and v7.3 (h5py) `data_structure` files; `load_motion_energy` handles the three motion-energy file variants.\n- Ports of the reference MATLAB routines: `time_axis` (getSeq.m), `gausswin`/`causal_kernel`/`mysmooth` (mySmooth.m), `bin_spikes` (alignSpikes.m + getSeq.m), `interp_to_axis`/`_fill_nearest` (interp1 + fillmissing('nearest')), `speed_from_xy` (findVelocity.m).\n- `process_session`: trial curation, neural binning, unit curation, behavioural outputs, video outputs, per-session discretization.\n- `plot_processing`: 14-panel figure per session covering every processing step.\n- `main`: multiprocessing pool over sessions, assembly, session curation, metadata, pickling.\n\nEfficiency:\n- Spike binning vectorised with `np.histogram2d` over (trial, aligned time) per unit instead of a per-trial loop (the reference's double loop over units x trials).\n- Smoothing done with `scipy.signal.fftconvolve` over all trials at once.\n- Video frames binned with `np.bincount` instead of per-bin loops.\n- Sessions processed in parallel with a `multiprocessing.Pool` (default 8 workers; memory-bound because v7.3 files are 90-250 MB each).\n\nCode inefficiencies identified: per-trial DLC reads from HDF5 dominate runtime (each trial is a separate dataset reference).\nCode speedups added: vectorised histogram binning, FFT smoothing, bincount frame binning, multiprocessing over sessions.\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nRan `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing` (sessions JEB6_2021-04-18 and JEB11_2022-05-10) -> `/app/conversion_sample_out.txt`, then `train_decoder.py --verify-only` -> `/app/verification_sample_out.txt` (**valid, no errors, no warnings**).\n\n### Sample Statistics\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Sessions | 2 |\n| Neurons (total) | 92 (29 + 63) |\n| Trials (total) | 625 (302 + 323) |\n| Trials / session | 302, 323 (of 382, 365 raw; The lowest ratios are the two kinematic outputs (tongue 1.83x, paw 1.84x), which is expected: they are time-varying, single-bin movement labels decoded by a *linear, memoryless* model from 100 PCs, and the medians are computed per session so the classes are exactly balanced (a hard 3-way problem).\n\n### Check 2: Accuracy comparison to the paper\nThe paper trains a **separate** logistic-regression model at each time bin with balanced classes; the provided decoder trains a **single** model shared over all timepoints, sessions, and trial types, so the numbers are not directly comparable. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 mapping table: \"side-cam `tongue` x/y (`obj.traj{1}`) -> `output[3]` = `tongue_velocity` | speed=|d(x,y)/dt| of interpolated position; 0 if < session median, 1 if >= median, 2 if tongue not visible (DLC NaN) | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m\". Step 2 lists the available features per view, and Step 5 decision 7 states that \"Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`\", because the decoder spec requires an explicit 'not visible' category. `tongue` is the first entry of `params.traj_features{1}` in every reference script. The notes do not explicitly argue against also using the bottom-camera tongue markers.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue velocity*?\n\ni. Four steps. (1) Frames where x or y is NaN (DLC low likelihood) are marked invisible. (2) Within each **contiguous run of visible frames**, x and y are differentiated with `np.gradient` (one-sided at run ends) and the speed is `hypot(vx, vy)`, then divided by the trial's median frame interval to give pixels/s; positions are not smoothed (matching `findPosition.m`, which skips smoothing for tongue features). A run of length 1 gets speed 0. (3) Frames are mapped to bins with `np.digitize` on the shared `edges` and the per-frame speeds are **averaged within each bin** by `np.bincount`; a bin is marked visible if it contains at least one visible frame, otherwise it is NaN/not-visible. (4) The binned speed is discretised at the session median (7-c). No cross-camera normalisation is needed since only one view is used; values stay in raw pixels/s.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef speed_from_xy(xy):\n    \"\"\"Speed of a DLC feature, computed like findVelocity.m (gradient of position),\n    but evaluated separately within each contiguous run of frames in which the\n    feature is visible.\n    ...\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = np.isfinite(xy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(xy[:, 1])\n    spd = np.full(xy.shape[0], np.nan)\n    ...\n    for a, b in zip(starts, stops):\n        seg = idx[a:b + 1]\n        if seg.size == 1:\n            spd[seg] = 0.0                      # single visible frame: no motion estimate\n            continue\n        vx = np.gradient(xy[seg, 0])\n        vy = np.gradient(xy[seg, 1])\n        spd[seg] = np.sqrt(vx ** 2 + vy ** 2)\n    return spd\n```\n\n```python\ndef _accumulate(idx, inb, spd, vis, spd_out, vis_out, trial, nbins):\n    \"\"\"Average per-frame speed within each time bin; a bin is visible if any frame is.\"\"\"\n    good = inb & vis & np.isfinite(spd)\n    if good.any():\n        sums = np.bincount(idx[good], weights=spd[good], minlength=nbins)\n        cnts = np.bincount(idx[good], minlength=nbins)\n        ...\n        spd_out[trial] = vals\n        vis_out[trial] = cnts > 0\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 10 Check 2 documents that the run-wise gradient was a **bug fix** found by the sanity checks: \"the initial `speed_from_xy` used `np.gradient` over the whole trial, so visible frames adjacent to a NaN frame received a NaN speed and were mislabelled 'not visible' (tongue 'not visible' was 0.845 -> 0.826 after the fix; ~2% of visible timepoints were affected). Fixed by computing the gradient separately inside each contiguous run of visible frames.\" Step 10 Check 3(f) records the deliberate differences from the reference: \"(i) DLC NaNs become the 'not visible' class instead of being filled ..., (ii) speed = |velocity| rather than separate x/y velocities, discretized at the session median (required by the decoder spec)\".\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Tongue velocity* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. A single per-session threshold: the 50th percentile of the binned tongue speed pooled over **all kept trials and all bins in which the tongue is visible** (invisible bins are excluded from the percentile). Bins with speed < threshold -> 0, >= threshold -> 1, invisible (or outside video coverage, or trial without usable video) -> 2. The threshold is recorded per session in `metadata['session_info'][i]['thresholds']`. Result: 0.087 / 0.087 / 0.826 overall — the two visible classes are equal to three decimals, as a median split requires.\n\nii.\n```python\n    sel = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=bool)\n    sel[trials] = True\n    m_t = sel[:, None] & tongue_vis & np.isfinite(tongue_spd)\n    thr_t = np.nanpercentile(tongue_spd[m_t], 50) if m_t.any() else np.nan\n    ...\n    tongue_cls = discretize(tongue_spd, tongue_vis, thr_t)\n```\n\n```python\ndef discretize(values, visible, thresh):\n    \"\"\"0 = below threshold, 1 = at/above threshold, 2 = not visible / no video.\"\"\"\n    out = np.full(values.shape, 2, dtype=np.int64)\n    v = visible & np.isfinite(values)\n    out[v & (values < thresh)] = 0\n    out[v & (values >= thresh)] = 1\n    return out\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 8: \"**Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\" Step 7: \"Discretization: class 0 and class 1 fractions are equal to 3 decimals for every discretized output (median split), as expected\"; Step 10 Check 2: \"discretized outputs are balanced 50/50 between class 0 and 1 | 9 | PASS\". Step 9 checks the not-visible fraction against the raw data: \"tongue visible only during licking | DLC NaN = not visible | ~89% NaN over the whole trial | not visible 0.845 | YES\" (0.826 after the run-wise-gradient fix).\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Tongue velocity* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Two corrections, then the shared grid. First the video clock is put on the behaviour clock with the reference's `findVideoOffset.m` constant, computed once per session: `vidshift = mode(sglx.bitcode.bitstart)/sglx.fs − mode(bp.ev.bitStart)` (~0.49-0.50 s; NaNs removed from `bitstart` before taking the mode). A fifth filter is applied after the neural data are built: trials in which **no** curated unit fires a single spike anywhere in the 5 s window are dropped, because in JEB24_2023-10-23 (trials 292-319) and JEB24_2023-11-03 (trials 301-333) the probe recording ended while Bpod kept running. **Ignore trials are deliberately retained** (they are a required output class). The result is 13,762 kept trials of 15,062 (193-474 per session).\n\nii.\n```python\n    stim = s.bpvec('stim/enable') if s.has_bp_field('stim') else np.zeros(ntrials)\n    early = s.bpvec('early')\n    hit = s.bpvec('hit')\n    miss = s.bpvec('miss')\n    no = s.bpvec('no')\n    autowater = s.bpvec('autowater')\n    for v in (stim, early, hit, miss, no, autowater):\n        v[np.isnan(v)] = 0\n    keep = (stim[:ntrials] == 0) & (early[:ntrials] == 0) & np.isfinite(gocue[:ntrials])\n    # a trial must be one of hit / miss / ignore\n    keep &= (hit[:ntrials] + miss[:ntrials] + no[:ntrials]) > 0\n    trials = np.where(keep)[0]\n```\n\n```python\n    # Trials in which no curated unit fired a single spike in the whole 5 s window\n    # have no ephys coverage (in 2 JEB24 sessions the recording stopped before the\n    # behavioural session ended); drop them.\n    if nunits > 0:\n        has_spikes = rates[trials].sum(axis=(1, 2)) > 0\n        n_nospk = int((~has_spikes).sum())\n        trials = trials[has_spikes]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 6: \"exclude photoinactivation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) and early-lick trials (`bp.early`), exactly as every reference condition string does ('~stim.enable&~early') and as stated in the methods ... **Ignore trials are kept** because 'ignore' and 'none' are required output classes.\" The zero-spike filter was added in Step 9/10 in response to 61 verification warnings: \"First full run produced 61 warnings 'all neural data is zero' in JEB24_2023-10-23 (trials 292-319) and JEB24_2023-11-03 (trials 301-333). What variables in the raw data is the `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. `obj.clu{probe}` — the spike-sorted clusters of the probe(s) listed for that session in the authors' meta scripts. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. Aligned spike times are counted into the 30 ms bin grid with a single `np.histogram2d` over (trial, aligned time) per cluster, divided by the bin width to give spikes/s, then smoothed along time by a **causal** Gaussian kernel: `gausswin(15)` with its first half zeroed and renormalised, with the reference's `'reflect'` boundary handling (prepend the first 15 samples, convolve, trim). Nothing else is done: no z-scoring, no baseline subtraction, no normalisation; stored values are firing rates in Hz as `float32`. Smoothing is applied to all trials at once with `scipy.signal.fftconvolve`.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef gausswin(N, alpha=2.5):\n    \"\"\"MATLAB gausswin(N, alpha).\"\"\"\n    n = np.arange(N) - (N - 1) / 2.0\n    return np.exp(-0.5 * (alpha * n / ((N - 1) / 2.0)) ** 2)\n\n\ndef causal_kernel(N=SMOOTH):\n    \"\"\"mySmooth.m kernel: gausswin with the first half zeroed (causal), normalized.\"\"\"\n    k = gausswin(N)\n    k[:N // 2] = 0.0\n    return k / k.sum()\n\n\ndef mysmooth(x, N=SMOOTH, bctype='reflect'):\n    \"\"\"Port of utils/mySmooth.m; smooths along axis 0.\"\"\"\n    ...\n    if bctype == 'reflect':\n        xf = np.concatenate([x[:N], x], axis=0)\n        trim = N\n    ...\n    out = fftconvolve(xf, k.reshape((-1,) + (1,) * (xf.ndim - 1)), mode='same', axes=0)\n    return out[trim:]\n```\n\n```python\n        cnt, _, _ = np.histogram2d(tr, aligned, bins=[trial_edges, edges])\n        meanfr[i] = cnt.sum() / (ntrials * window)\n        rates[:, :, i] = mysmooth(cnt.T / DT).T.astype(np.float32)\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 3: \"**Causal Gaussian smoothing, N=15 bins, 'reflect'** exactly as `mySmooth` — causal so no information from the future leaks backwards in time (important for a decoder).\" Step 1 records the reference chain `alignSpikes -> getSeq -> mySmooth` and `params.smooth = 15`, `bctype='reflect'`. Step 10 Check 2 verified the rate of 9 (trial, neuron) pairs against an independent from-scratch `np.convolve` recomputation from the raw spike times (`np.allclose`, PASS), and Check 3 records binning/smoothing as identical to `getSeq.m`. The addendum reports an empirical check that the chosen (dt=30 ms, smooth=15) setting beat (dt=10 ms, smooth=15) and (dt=30 ms, smooth=7) on every decoder output.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Three filters. (1) Manual curation label: the label is stripped and lower-cased and the cluster is dropped if it is in `{garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, ''}` — i.e. the `findClusters.m` `quality='all'` drop list plus unlabelled clusters; everything else is kept, including `poor`, `fair` and `multi`. (2) Mean firing rate: a unit is kept only if its mean rate over the whole −2.5..2.5 s window, computed from the **raw unsmoothed** counts pooled over all trials, exceeds 1 Hz (`removeLowFRClusters.m` with `params.lowFR = 1`; paper: \"all units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"). (3) Probe selection: only clusters on the probe(s) listed in the authors' meta scripts. A session-level filter (>=10 units) follows. Result: 2,457 units of ~14,300 raw clusters, 17-141 per session, mean 55.8.\n\nii.\n```python\nLOW_FR = 1.0          # params.lowFR (spikes/s); paper: \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"\nMIN_UNITS = 10        # paper: \"sessions were included ... only if they had at least 10 units\"\nBAD_QUALITY = {'garbage', 'gabrga', 'noisy', 'real?', ''}   # findClusters.m, quality='all'\n```\n\n```python\n            q = c['quality'].strip().lower()\n            if q in BAD_QUALITY:\n                continue                      # findClusters.m with quality = 'all'\n```\n\n```python\n    # removeLowFRClusters.m: mean rate must exceed lowFR (1 spk/s)\n    keep_units = meanfr > LOW_FR\n    rates = rates[:, :, keep_units]\n    cl_region = [r for r, k in zip(cl_region, keep_units) if k]\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 4: \"quality not in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, empty} (findClusters, case-insensitive/trimmed to handle label case and typos) AND mean firing rate over the trial window > 1 Hz (removeLowFRClusters with `lowFR=1`, matching the paper's 'units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz'). Sessions with < 10 units would be dropped (paper criterion); in practice all 44 pass.\" Step 2 justifies case-insensitive matching: \"Quality strings differ in case/padding between sessions ('Poor' vs 'poor   '), and include typos\". How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. What is the temporal resolution (time bin size) of the converted data? Is any temporal rebinning applied?\n\ni. 30 ms bins (`DT = 0.03`, `params.dt = (1/100)*3` from the paper's Figure 3 scripts), giving **166 bins per trial** for every trial of every session. The grid is built exactly as `getSeq.m` does: `edges = tmin:dt:tmax` and `time = edges + dt/2` with the last element dropped. Because 5 s is not an integer multiple of 30 ms, the edges run −2.5 to +2.48 s and the bin centres from −2.485 to +2.465 s (so the last ~20 ms of the nominal window is not covered, although `metadata['off_end']` is reported as 2.5). Spikes are binned directly at this resolution — there is no rebinning of a finer representation; the video and motion-energy streams are averaged/interpolated onto the same 166-bin axis, so all streams share one time axis. Neural smoothing is 15 bins of causal Gaussian, i.e. 450 ms at this bin width.\n\nii.\n```python\nTMIN = -2.5           # params.tmin\nTMAX = 2.5            # params.tmax\nDT = 0.03             # params.dt = (1/100)*3  (30 ms bins)\nSMOOTH = 15           # params.smooth (causal gaussian kernel width in bins)\n```\n\n```python\ndef time_axis():\n    \"\"\"getSeq.m: edges = tmin:dt:tmax; time = edges + dt/2 with the last dropped.\"\"\"\n    nedges = int(np.floor((TMAX - TMIN) / DT)) + 1\n    edges = TMIN + DT * np.arange(nedges)\n    t = edges + DT / 2.0\n    return edges, t[:-1]\n```\n\n```python\n        time_bin_size=DT * 1000.0,\n        ...\n        off_start=TMIN, off_end=TMAX,\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 2: \"**Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\" Step 3 records the ambiguity in the reference (\"`dt` = 5-30 ms depending on script ... CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 mapping table: \"side-cam `tongue` x/y (`obj.traj{1}`) -> `output[3]` = `tongue_velocity` | speed=|d(x,y)/dt| of interpolated position; 0 if < session median, 1 if >= median, 2 if tongue not visible (DLC NaN) | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m\". Step 2 lists the available features per view, and Step 5 decision 7 states that \"Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`\", because the decoder spec requires an explicit 'not visible' category. `tongue` is the first entry of `params.traj_features{1}` in every reference script. The notes do not explicitly argue against also using the bottom-camera tongue markers.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue velocity*?\n\ni. Four steps. (1) Frames where x or y is NaN (DLC low likelihood) are marked invisible. (2) Within each **contiguous run of visible frames**, x and y are differentiated with `np.gradient` (one-sided at run ends) and the speed is `hypot(vx, vy)`, then divided by the trial's median frame interval to give pixels/s; positions are not smoothed (matching `findPosition.m`, which skips smoothing for tongue features). A run of length 1 gets speed 0. (3) Frames are mapped to bins with `np.digitize` on the shared `edges` and the per-frame speeds are **averaged within each bin** by `np.bincount`; a bin is marked visible if it contains at least one visible frame, otherwise it is NaN/not-visible. (4) The binned speed is discretised at the session median (7-c). No cross-camera normalisation is needed since only one view is used; values stay in raw pixels/s.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef speed_from_xy(xy):\n    \"\"\"Speed of a DLC feature, computed like findVelocity.m (gradient of position),\n    but evaluated separately within each contiguous run of frames in which the\n    feature is visible.\n    ...\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = np.isfinite(xy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(xy[:, 1])\n    spd = np.full(xy.shape[0], np.nan)\n    ...\n    for a, b in zip(starts, stops):\n        seg = idx[a:b + 1]\n        if seg.size == 1:\n            spd[seg] = 0.0                      # single visible frame: no motion estimate\n            continue\n        vx = np.gradient(xy[seg, 0])\n        vy = np.gradient(xy[seg, 1])\n        spd[seg] = np.sqrt(vx ** 2 + vy ** 2)\n    return spd\n```\n\n```python\ndef _accumulate(idx, inb, spd, vis, spd_out, vis_out, trial, nbins):\n    \"\"\"Average per-frame speed within each time bin; a bin is visible if any frame is.\"\"\"\n    good = inb & vis & np.isfinite(spd)\n    if good.any():\n        sums = np.bincount(idx[good], weights=spd[good], minlength=nbins)\n        cnts = np.bincount(idx[good], minlength=nbins)\n        ...\n        spd_out[trial] = vals\n        vis_out[trial] = cnts > 0\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 10 Check 2 documents that the run-wise gradient was a **bug fix** found by the sanity checks: \"the initial `speed_from_xy` used `np.gradient` over the whole trial, so visible frames adjacent to a NaN frame received a NaN speed and were mislabelled 'not visible' (tongue 'not visible' was 0.845 -> 0.826 after the fix; ~2% of visible timepoints were affected). Fixed by computing the gradient separately inside each contiguous run of visible frames.\" Step 10 Check 3(f) records the deliberate differences from the reference: \"(i) DLC NaNs become the 'not visible' class instead of being filled ..., (ii) speed = |velocity| rather than separate x/y velocities, discretized at the session median (required by the decoder spec)\".\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Tongue velocity* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. A single per-session threshold: the 50th percentile of the binned tongue speed pooled over **all kept trials and all bins in which the tongue is visible** (invisible bins are excluded from the percentile). Bins with speed < threshold -> 0, >= threshold -> 1, invisible (or outside video coverage, or trial without usable video) -> 2. The threshold is recorded per session in `metadata['session_info'][i]['thresholds']`. Result: 0.087 / 0.087 / 0.826 overall — the two visible classes are equal to three decimals, as a median split requires.\n\nii.\n```python\n    sel = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=bool)\n    sel[trials] = True\n    m_t = sel[:, None] & tongue_vis & np.isfinite(tongue_spd)\n    thr_t = np.nanpercentile(tongue_spd[m_t], 50) if m_t.any() else np.nan\n    ...\n    tongue_cls = discretize(tongue_spd, tongue_vis, thr_t)\n```\n\n```python\ndef discretize(values, visible, thresh):\n    \"\"\"0 = below threshold, 1 = at/above threshold, 2 = not visible / no video.\"\"\"\n    out = np.full(values.shape, 2, dtype=np.int64)\n    v = visible & np.isfinite(values)\n    out[v & (values < thresh)] = 0\n    out[v & (values >= thresh)] = 1\n    return out\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 8: \"**Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\" Step 7: \"Discretization: class 0 and class 1 fractions are equal to 3 decimals for every discretized output (median split), as expected\"; Step 10 Check 2: \"discretized outputs are balanced 50/50 between class 0 and 1 | 9 | PASS\". Step 9 checks the not-visible fraction against the raw data: \"tongue visible only during licking | DLC NaN = not visible | ~89% NaN over the whole trial | not visible 0.845 | YES\" (0.826 after the run-wise-gradient fix).\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *Tongue velocity* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Two corrections, then the shared grid. The side camera's own `frameTimes` are used, since the tongue comes from the side camera.\n\nii.\n```python\n    def vidshift(self):\n        \"\"\"funcs/findVideoOffset.m: mode(sglx.bitcode.bitstart)/fs - mode(bp.ev.bitStart)\"\"\"\n        from scipy.stats import mode as _mode\n        bitStart = _mode(self.ev('bitStart'), keepdims=False).mode\n        ...\n        bs = bs[~np.isnan(bs)]\n        return float(_mode(bs, keepdims=False).mode / fs - bitStart)\n```\n\n```python\n        # video clock -> time from the alignment event\n        vt0 = ft0 - vidshift - gocue[i]\n        dtf = np.median(np.diff(ft0)) if ft0.size > 1 else 1 / 400.0\n        has_video[i] = True\n        idx = np.digitize(vt0, bin_edges) - 1               # bin index for each frame\n        inb = (idx >= 0) & (idx < nbins)\n```\n\niii. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Motion energy*?\n\ni. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Every known quirk is handled by keeping the trial/session and marking or repairing the specific gap:\n- **Two MATLAB file formats**: `is_hdf5` sniffs the header; `h5py` for v7.3 (36 files), `scipy.io` for v7 (11 files), behind one accessor API; What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Three loops remain. (1) The per-cluster loop in `bin_spikes` — each cluster has its own ragged spike list, but the trial dimension inside it is already vectorised by `histogram2d` and smoothing is applied to all trials at once with `fftconvolve`. (2) The per-trial video loop in `process_session` — each trial has a different number of camera frames, so there is no rectangular array to work on; within a trial the frame-to-bin reduction is vectorised with `np.digitize` + `np.bincount`. (3) The per-run loop inside `speed_from_xy`, needed so gradients never cross a visibility gap. (4) The per-trial `lick_dir` loop over ragged lick-time cells. Sessions themselves are run in parallel processes rather than serially.\n\nii.\n```python\n        cnt, _, _ = np.histogram2d(tr, aligned, bins=[trial_edges, edges])\n        meanfr[i] = cnt.sum() / (ntrials * window)\n        rates[:, :, i] = mysmooth(cnt.T / DT).T.astype(np.float32)\n```\n\n```python\n        sums = np.bincount(idx[good], weights=spd[good], minlength=nbins)\n        cnts = np.bincount(idx[good], minlength=nbins)\n```\n\n```python\n        with Pool(nproc) as pool:\n            results = pool.map(_worker, list(zip(sessions, want_debug)))\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 6: \"Spike binning vectorised with `np.histogram2d` over (trial, aligned time) per unit instead of a per-trial loop (the reference's double loop over units x trials). Smoothing done with `scipy.signal.fftconvolve` over all trials at once. Video frames binned with `np.bincount` instead of per-bin loops. Sessions processed in parallel with a `multiprocessing.Pool` (default 8 workers; memory-bound because v7.3 files are 90-250 MB each).\" Step 7: \"vectorised histogram2d binning + FFT smoothing + bincount + 8-way multiprocessing | ~10x vs naive loops\".\n\n## 11-c. What processing does the code repeat multiple times?\n\ni. Little, but not nothing. Each file is read once per session; `vidshift` is computed once per session (not per trial); the bin grid is rebuilt by `time_axis()` in each session and again in `main`, which is trivial. The genuine repeats are: `s.probe_locs()` is re-read inside the probe loop rather than once before it; `causal_kernel()` is rebuilt on every `mysmooth` call, i.e. once per cluster; the `ts` array of a trial is read twice per camera-bearing stream in the sense that the full feature array is materialised and then indexed per feature; and `speed_from_xy` recomputes the visibility mask that the caller also computes. Neural smoothing is 15 bins of causal Gaussian, i.e. 450 ms at this bin width.\n\nii.\n```python\nTMIN = -2.5           # params.tmin\nTMAX = 2.5            # params.tmax\nDT = 0.03             # params.dt = (1/100)*3  (30 ms bins)\nSMOOTH = 15           # params.smooth (causal gaussian kernel width in bins)\n```\n\n```python\ndef time_axis():\n    \"\"\"getSeq.m: edges = tmin:dt:tmax; time = edges + dt/2 with the last dropped.\"\"\"\n    nedges = int(np.floor((TMAX - TMIN) / DT)) + 1\n    edges = TMIN + DT * np.arange(nedges)\n    t = edges + DT / 2.0\n    return edges, t[:-1]\n```\n\n```python\n        time_bin_size=DT * 1000.0,\n        ...\n        off_start=TMIN, off_end=TMAX,\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 2: \"**Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\" Step 3 records the ambiguity in the reference (\"`dt` = 5-30 ms depending on script ... CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 mapping table: \"side-cam `tongue` x/y (`obj.traj{1}`) -> `output[3]` = `tongue_velocity` | speed=|d(x,y)/dt| of interpolated position; 0 if < session median, 1 if >= median, 2 if tongue not visible (DLC NaN) | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m\". The notes do not explicitly argue against also using the bottom-camera tongue markers.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *Tongue velocity*?\n\ni. Four steps. (1) Frames where x or y is NaN (DLC low likelihood) are marked invisible. (2) Within each **contiguous run of visible frames**, x and y are differentiated with `np.gradient` (one-sided at run ends) and the speed is `hypot(vx, vy)`, then divided by the trial's median frame interval to give pixels/s; positions are not smoothed (matching `findPosition.m`, which skips smoothing for tongue features). A run of length 1 gets speed 0. (3) Frames are mapped to bins with `np.digitize` on the shared `edges` and the per-frame speeds are **averaged within each bin** by `np.bincount`; a bin is marked visible if it contains at least one visible frame, otherwise it is NaN/not-visible. (4) The binned speed is discretised at the session median (7-c). No cross-camera normalisation is needed since only one view is used; values stay in raw pixels/s.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef speed_from_xy(xy):\n    \"\"\"Speed of a DLC feature, computed like findVelocity.m (gradient of position),\n    but evaluated separately within each contiguous run of frames in which the\n    feature is visible.\n    ...\n    \"\"\"\n    vis = np.isfinite(xy[:, 0]) & np.isfinite(xy[:, 1])\n    spd = np.full(xy.shape[0], np.nan)\n    ...\n    for a, b in zip(starts, stops):\n        seg = idx[a:b + 1]\n        if seg.size == 1:\n            spd[seg] = 0.0                      # single visible frame: no motion estimate\n            continue\n        vx = np.gradient(xy[seg, 0])\n        vy = np.gradient(xy[seg, 1])\n        spd[seg] = np.sqrt(vx ** 2 + vy ** 2)\n    return spd\n```\n\n```python\ndef _accumulate(idx, inb, spd, vis, spd_out, vis_out, trial, nbins):\n    \"\"\"Average per-frame speed within each time bin; a bin is visible if any frame is.\"\"\"\n    good = inb & vis & np.isfinite(spd)\n    if good.any():\n        sums = np.bincount(idx[good], weights=spd[good], minlength=nbins)\n        cnts = np.bincount(idx[good], minlength=nbins)\n        ...\n        spd_out[trial] = vals\n        vis_out[trial] = cnts > 0\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 10 Check 2 documents that the run-wise gradient was a **bug fix** found by the sanity checks: \"the initial `speed_from_xy` used `np.gradient` over the whole trial, so visible frames adjacent to a NaN frame received a NaN speed and were mislabelled 'not visible' (tongue 'not visible' was 0.845 -> 0.826 after the fix; ~2% of visible timepoints were affected). Fixed by computing the gradient separately inside each contiguous run of visible frames.\" Step 10 Check 3(f) records the deliberate differences from the reference: \"(i) DLC NaNs become the 'not visible' class instead of being filled ..., (ii) speed = |velocity| rather than separate x/y velocities, discretized at the session median (required by the decoder spec)\".\n\n## 7-c. How is `output` *Tongue velocity* thresholded into categories?\n\ni. A single per-session threshold: the 50th percentile of the binned tongue speed pooled over **all kept trials and all bins in which the tongue is visible** (invisible bins are excluded from the percentile). Bins with speed < threshold -> 0, >= threshold -> 1, invisible (or outside video coverage, or trial without usable video) -> 2. The threshold is recorded per session in `metadata['session_info'][i]['thresholds']`. Result: 0.087 / 0.087 / 0.826 overall — the two visible classes are equal to three decimals, as a median split requires.\n\nii.\n```python\n    sel = np.zeros(ntrials, dtype=bool)\n    sel[trials] = True\n    m_t = sel[:, None] & tongue_vis & np.isfinite(tongue_spd)\n    thr_t = np.nanpercentile(tongue_spd[m_t], 50) if m_t.any() else np.nan\n    ...\n    tongue_cls = discretize(tongue_spd, tongue_vis, thr_t)\n```\n\n```python\ndef discretize(values, visible, thresh):\n    \"\"\"0 = below threshold, 1 = at/above threshold, 2 = not visible / no video.\"\"\"\n    out = np.full(values.shape, 2, dtype=np.int64)\n    v = visible & np.isfinite(values)\n    out[v & (values < thresh)] = 0\n    out[v & (values >= thresh)] = 1\n    return out\n```\n\niii. CONVERSION_NOTES.md Step 5 decision 8: \"**Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\" Step 7: \"Discretization: class 0 and class 1 fractions are equal to 3 decimals for every discretized output (median split), as expected\"; Step 10 Check 2: \"discretized outputs are balanced 50/50 between class 0 and 1 | 9 | PASS\". How are **all the data** for all subjects, sessions, and trials loaded in?\n\ni. Each session is one MATLAB file, `data_structure_<anm>_<date>.mat`, split across two folders (`Ephys_Behavior` and `RandomizedDelay_Ephys_Behavior`), with its motion energy in a `motionEnergy_<anm>_<date>.mat` beside it. The sessions are not discovered by globbing: the 44 session names and the probe each one uses are hard-coded in `SESSIONS`, transcribed from the authors' own loading scripts. Each session is opened once by `load_mat`, which reads the v7.3 files with `h5py` and the v5 files with `scipy.io`.\n\nii. The session list and the loop over it:\n```python\nSESSIONS = {\n    'EKH1_2021-08-07': [2],\n    ...\n    'JEB24_2023-11-03': [1],\n}\n\nfor i, name in enumerate(names, 1):\n    res = process_session(name)\n```\n\nLoading one session:\n```python\ndef load_mat(path):\n    try:\n        with h5py.File(path, 'r') as f:\n            return _h5(f, f['obj'])\n    except OSError:\n        return scipy.io.loadmat(path, simplify_cells=True)['obj']\n```\n\niii. The authors' `load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m` files are the definitive record of which sessions and which probe entered their analysis, and several files in the data folders are either commented out there or absent from it, so globbing the folders would pull in sessions the paper excluded. Both MATLAB formats appear in the shared data, so both readers are needed.\n\n## 1-b. How are the data split into subjects?\n\ni. The animal is the part of the session name before the underscore, so `JEB19_2023-04-19` belongs to subject `JEB19`. That string is carried through as the session's subject, and at assembly `subjects` is the sorted set of unique animals with `subject_idx` giving each session's index into it. The 44 sessions come from 14 animals.\n\nii. Per session:\n```python\nreturn {\n    'session_id': name,\n    'subject': name.split('_')[0],\n    ...\n```\n\nAt assembly:\n```python\nsubjects = sorted({r['subject'] for r in results})\nsub_ix = {s: i for i, s in enumerate(subjects)}\n...\n'subjects': subjects,\n'subject_idx': np.array([sub_ix[r['subject']] for r in results], np.int32),\n```\n\niii. The animal id is not stored consistently inside the files — `obj.meta.anm` is missing from several sessions — but it is always in the filename, which is also how the authors' own loading scripts identify animals.\n\n## 1-c. How are the data split into sessions?\n\ni. One session is one entry in `SESSIONS`, keyed by `<anm>_<date>`, and one file on disk. `session_file` finds which of the two task folders holds it, so the fixed-delay and randomized-delay sessions are treated uniformly rather than as two datasets. Each becomes one element of `neural`, `input`, and `output`. The result is 44 sessions: 25 fixed-delay and 19 randomized-delay.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef session_file(name, prefix):\n    \"\"\"Path to the data_structure or motionEnergy file of a session.\"\"\"\n    for folder in EPHYS:\n        path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, folder, '%s_%s.mat' % (prefix, name))\n        if os.path.exists(path):\n            return path\n    raise FileNotFoundError('%s_%s.mat' % (prefix, name))\n```\n\niii. The sessions are the ones listed in the authors' `load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m` files, as in 1-a.\n\n## 1-d. Are the data correctly split into trials?\n\ni. Yes. Every per-trial field of `obj.bp` has `Ntrials` entries and one go cue, so a trial is one row of that table and one entry of `bp.ev.goCue`. `trial_column` reads any of those fields and truncates to `Ntrials`, since a few fields are stored longer than the trial count. Spike times and camera frames both carry the trial they belong to, so no trial boundaries have to be reconstructed.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef trial_column(bp, *names):\n    \"\"\"One entry per trial from a field of bp, e.g. trial_column(bp, 'stim', 'enable').\"\"\"\n    n_trials = int(np.ravel(bp['Ntrials'])[0])\n    field = bp\n    for name in names:\n        field = field[name]\n    return np.ravel(np.asarray(field, float))[:n_trials]\n```\n\niii. The Bpod table defines the trials directly and there is exactly one go cue per trial, so no inference is needed.\n\n## 1-e. How are trials filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Three filters, all applied before anything is computed. Early-lick trials (`bp.early`) and photostimulation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) are dropped, following the paper, which omits early licks from all analyses and treats photoinactivation as a separate experiment. Then trials that run past the end of the recording are dropped: in two sessions the behaviour continues after the probe stops, leaving trials with no spikes at all, and `haveEphys` does not flag them, so the cutoff is taken from the last trial in which any surviving unit fires. Across the dataset this keeps 13,762 of 15,155 trials.\n\nii. Early lick and photostim, in `trial_info`:\n```python\nearly = trial_column(bp, 'early') > 0\nstim = trial_column(bp, 'stim', 'enable') > 0\n...\nreturn info[~early & ~stim]\n```\n\nRecording length, in `Neural.__init__` and `process_session`:\n```python\nlast = max(int(np.asarray(cluster['trial'], int).max(initial=0))\n           for cluster in self.clusters)\nself.trials = np.asarray([t for t in trials if t < last])   # trial numbers are 1 based\n...\ninfo = info.loc[neural.trials]                 # drops any trial past the recording\n```\n\niii. Early-lick and photostim removal follows the paper. The recording-length cut is needed because a trial after the probe stops would otherwise enter the dataset as 1000 bins of zero firing across every neuron.\n\n## 2-a. What variables in the raw data is the final `neural` data derived from?\n\ni. `obj.clu{probe}`, the spike-sorted clusters. Each cluster carries `trial` (the trial each spike falls in, 1-based), `trialtm` (the spike time relative to that trial's start), and `quality` (the manual curation label). The go cue times `bp.ev.goCue` are the other input, since they set the alignment.\n\nii. Those fields become the spike counts:\n```python\ndef spike_count(self, cluster):\n    \"\"\"Spikes of one cluster per trial and bin, aligned to the go cue.\"\"\"\n    spike_trial = np.asarray(cluster['trial'], int) - 1         # trial numbers are 1 based\n    spike_time = np.asarray(cluster['trialtm'], float) - self.go_cue[spike_trial]\n\n    # count spikes into a trial by bin grid; those outside the window fall off the edges\n    trial_edges = np.arange(self.go_cue.size + 1) - 0.5\n    counts, _, _ = np.histogram2d(spike_trial, spike_time, bins=[trial_edges, BIN_EDGES])\n    return counts[self.trials]                                  # only the trials we keep\n```\n\niii. `trialtm` is already on the behaviour clock and relative to trial start, so subtracting the go cue of its own trial is the only conversion needed. Counting every spike into a trial by bin grid in one call means spikes outside the window need no explicit handling, and the dropped trials are removed afterwards by selecting rows.\n\n## 2-b. How is the `neural` data processed?\n\ni. The counts from 2-a are divided by the bin width to give spikes/s, then smoothed along time with a Gaussian of 14 ms standard deviation. Nothing else is done — no normalisation, no baseline subtraction, no z-scoring — so the stored values are firing rates in Hz. Units from both probes of a two-probe session are concatenated into one population.\n\nii.\n```python\nsigma = RATE_SD_MS / 1000 / BIN\nrates = []\nfor cluster in self.clusters:\n    rate = self.spike_count(cluster) / BIN                 # counts -> Hz\n    if rate.mean() > MIN_RATE:\n        rates.append(gaussian_filter1d(rate, sigma, axis=1, mode='reflect'))\n```\n\niii. 14 ms is the standard deviation of the reference's smoothing kernel: `params.smooth = 15` builds a `gausswin(15)`, whose sigma is `(15-1)/(2 × 2.5) = 2.8` samples, and at 5 ms bins that is 14 ms.\n\n## 2-c. How is the `neural` data filtered based on quality controls?\n\ni. Two filters. First the manual curation label `clu.quality`, lower-cased and matched against a drop list of `garbage`, `gabrga`, `noisy`, `real?`, and `poor` — everything else is kept, including multi-units. Then any unit whose mean rate over the window is at or below 1 Hz is dropped. Across the dataset this leaves 1,954 units of the 10,330 clusters on file, 15 to 110 per session.\n\nii.\n```python\nQUALITY_DROP = {'garbage', 'gabrga', 'noisy', 'real?', 'poor'}\nMIN_RATE = 1.0\n\ndef _quality(cluster):\n    \"\"\"Quality label of a cluster; a handful carry no label at all.\"\"\"\n    label = cluster['quality']\n    return label.strip().lower() if isinstance(label, str) else ''\n...\nself.clusters = [cluster for probe in probes                # probes concatenated\n                 for cluster in self._probe_clusters(probe)\n                 if _quality(cluster) not in QUALITY_DROP]\n...\nif rate.mean() > MIN_RATE:\n```\n\niii. The drop list follows the reference's `findClusters.m`, which excludes exactly `garbage`, `gabrga` (their typo for it), `noisy`, and `real?`; `poor` is dropped in addition. The label is free text written in either case and with typos, so it is matched lower-cased rather than exactly as the reference does. The 1 Hz cut is the paper's: \"all units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz were included in all other analyses\".\n\n## 2-d. How is the per-trial `neural` data aligned to the event described in the `instructions`?\n\ni. Alignment to the go cue is a single subtraction. `clu.trialtm` is already on the behaviour clock and already relative to its own trial's start, and `bp.ev.goCue` is on the same clock, so `trialtm − goCue[trial]` puts every spike in seconds from the go cue with no offset or interpolation. The camera streams need a clock correction first (see 6-c); the neural data does not.\n\nii.\n```python\nspike_trial = np.asarray(cluster['trial'], int) - 1         # trial numbers are 1 based\nspike_time = np.asarray(cluster['trialtm'], float) - self.go_cue[spike_trial]\n```\n\niii. How is the `neural` data temporally binned/resampled?\n\ni. Spikes are counted into 1000 non-overlapping 5 ms bins spanning −2.5 to +2.5 s from the go cue. The grid is built once at module level and is the same for every trial, session, and stream, so the neural data, the input, and the three camera outputs all share one time axis.\n\nii.\n```python\nT_START, T_STOP = -2.5, 2.5     # time window around the go cue (match the paper)\nBIN = 0.005\nN_BINS = int(round((T_STOP - T_START) / BIN))             # 1000\nBIN_EDGES = T_START + BIN * np.arange(N_BINS + 1)\nTIME = BIN_EDGES[:-1] + BIN / 2                           # bin centres, the only input\n```\n\niii. 5 ms is the reference's `params.dt = 1/200`, and −2.5 to 2.5 s is its `params.tmin`/`params.tmax`.\n\n## 3-a. What variables in the raw data is `input` *time_from_go_cue* derived from?\n\ni. This variable is defined by us based on the go cue of each trial, which is the event every trial is aligned on. Two per-trial fields of `obj.bp`: the instructed side, `R` (with `L` its complement), and the outcome flags `hit` and `miss`. A hit means the animal licked the instructed port, a miss means it licked the other one, and anything else means it did not lick. So the class is the instructed side on hit trials, the opposite side on miss trials, and a third class, `no lick`, everywhere else. Codes are left 0, right 1, no lick 2.\n\nii.\n```python\nLICK = {'left': 0, 'right': 1, 'no lick': 2}\n...\n# a hit licks the instructed port, a miss licks the other one, an ignore neither\nlick_direction = np.full(n_trials, LICK['no lick'])\nlick_direction[hit] = np.where(right[hit], LICK['right'], LICK['left'])\nlick_direction[miss] = np.where(right[miss], LICK['left'], LICK['right'])\n```\n\niii. What variables in the raw data is `output` *tongue_velocity* derived from?\n\ni. The DeepLabCut tracking in `obj.traj`, which holds one entry per camera.
