Both cameras are used because the tongue is visible in only a small fraction of frames and the two views disagree about which ones — on the example trial the bottom camera tracked it in 192 frames and the side camera in 93 — so using both recovers more of the lick bout than either alone.\n\n## 7-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *tongue_velocity*?\n\ni. Five steps. **(1)** Frames whose likelihood is at or below 0.9 are dropped; the authors already set x and y to NaN there, so this is the visibility rule already in the data. **(2)** Within each contiguous run of surviving frames, x and y are smoothed with a 5 ms Gaussian and differentiated against the real frame times, and the speed is the magnitude of the two derivatives. **(3)** Each camera's speed is averaged into the 5 ms bins. **(4)** Each is divided by its own 90th percentile over the whole session, then the two are averaged per bin, using whichever view is present when the other is missing. **(5)** The result is split at the session median into two classes, with a third class for bins where neither camera tracked the tongue.\n\nii. Velocity within a run:\n```python\nfor start, stop in _runs(valid):\n    if stop - start < 2:                       # a lone frame has no velocity\n        continue\n    sx = gaussian_filter1d(x[start:stop], sigma, mode='mirror')\n    sy = gaussian_filter1d(y[start:stop], sigma, mode='mirror')\n    speed[start:stop] = np.hypot(np.gradient(sx, time[start:stop]),\n                                 np.gradient(sy, time[start:stop]))\n```\n\nCombining the two cameras:\n```python\ndef tongue_velocity(self):\n    \"\"\"Binned tongue velocity, as (n_trials, N_BINS).\"\"\"\n    side = np.array([_bin_frames(*self.side_tongue[trial]) for trial in self.trials])\n    bottom = np.array([_bin_frames(*self.bottom_tongue[trial]) for trial in self.trials])\n    side = side / self.side_scale\n    bottom = bottom / self.bottom_scale\n    return _mean_over_available(side, bottom)      # one view alone where the other is missing\n```\n\n```python\n_discretize(tongue, np.nanpercentile(tongue, SPLIT_PCT))\n```\n\niii. We combine the information from the two camera view to get the speed estimate. The two views are on different pixel scales — the side camera's 90th percentile is roughly twice the bottom camera's — so they cannot be averaged raw; normalising each by its own percentile is the same device the paper uses for its kinematic overlays, where features are \"standardized by taking the 99th percentile across time and trials\". The 50th-percentile split is the prompt's. The `not visible` class is needed because the tongue is out of view in about 88% of bins.\n\n## 7-d. How is `output` *tongue_velocity* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. The camera runs on its own clock, which starts earlier than the behaviour clock, so `frameTimes` cannot be compared to the go cue directly. The offset is found once per session from the bitcode pulse that both streams record: where it sits in the recording file (`sglx.bitcode.bitstart / sglx.fs`) minus where it sits on the behaviour clock (`bp.ev.bitStart`), taking the mode of each. Frame time from the go cue is then `frameTimes − offset − goCue[trial]`. After that the frames are binned onto the same 5 ms grid as the spikes, so the two streams share one time axis.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef _video_offset(self):\n    \"\"\"Seconds by which the video clock leads the behavior clock (findVideoOffset.m).\"\"\"\n    sample_rate = float(np.ravel(self.obj['sglx']['fs'])[0])\n    video_start = np.ravel(self.obj['sglx']['bitcode']['bitstart']) / sample_rate\n    behavior_start = trial_column(self.obj['bp'], 'ev', 'bitStart')\n    return pd.Series(video_start).mode().iloc[0] - pd.Series(behavior_start).mode().iloc[0]\n\ndef _frame_time(self, trial, view):\n    \"\"\"Frame times of one trial and camera, in seconds from go cue onset.\"\"\"\n    frame_times = np.ravel(self._traj(trial, view)['frameTimes'])\n    return frame_times - self.offset - self.go_cue[trial]\n```\n\niii. This is the reference's `findVideoOffset.m`, and the offset is a session constant so it is computed once in `__init__` rather than per trial. Two checks: after the correction the frames start at −2.475 s from the go cue, just inside the window, and on the example trial the tongue is invisible for the entire delay and appears only after the go cue, with the first protrusion just before the recorded reward time.\n\n## 8-a. What variables in the raw data is `output` *paw_velocity* derived from?\n\ni. The same `obj.traj` tracking, but only the bottom camera and only `top_paw`. The bottom view tracks two paws, `top_paw` and `bottom_paw`; only the first is used.\n\nii.\n```python\nPAW = 'top_paw'                  # this is the reliable view for the paw tracking\n...\nself.paw = self._trial_velocity(PAW)\n```\n\niii. `bottom_paw` drops out through the delay epoch — its likelihood oscillates between 0.2 and 1.0 until about 0.4 s after the go cue, leaving it untracked in roughly half the window — whereas `top_paw` is tracked in essentially every frame. They are two different forepaws rather than two views of one, so they cannot be averaged the way the tongue views are; using the reliably tracked one avoids inventing a delay-epoch signal.\n\n## 8-b. What processing is involved in computing `output` *paw_velocity*?\n\ni. The same velocity computation as the tongue — likelihood cut, per-run Gaussian smoothing of x and y, speed as the magnitude of the two derivatives — then binning into 5 ms bins and a split at the session median, with a third class for untracked bins. No normalisation, since there is only one camera to reconcile, so the values stay in pixels per second.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef paw_velocity(self):\n    \"\"\"Binned paw velocity, as (n_trials, N_BINS).\"\"\"\n    return np.array([_bin_frames(*self.paw[trial]) for trial in self.trials])\n...\n_discretize(paw, np.nanpercentile(paw, SPLIT_PCT))\n```\n\niii. Normalisation exists only to make two cameras comparable, so it is skipped here. The `not visible` class still appears, on about 19% of bins, since tracking does fail on some trials entirely.\n\n## 8-d. How is `output` *paw_velocity* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Identically to the tongue: the session's video offset is subtracted from `frameTimes`, then the go cue of that trial, and the frames falling inside the window are binned onto the same 5 ms grid as the spikes. The paw comes from the bottom camera, so its own view's frame times are used.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef _frame_time(self, trial, view):\n    \"\"\"Frame times of one trial and camera, in seconds from go cue onset.\"\"\"\n    frame_times = np.ravel(self._traj(trial, view)['frameTimes'])\n    return frame_times - self.offset - self.go_cue[trial]\n```\n\nTrimmed to the window in `_track`:\n```python\ntime = self._frame_time(trial, view)           # frame counts can differ between views\ninside = (time >= T_START) & (time <= T_STOP)\nreturn time[inside], x[inside], y[inside], likelihood[inside]\n```\n\niii. Same offset and same grid as every other stream, so the paw needs no separate treatment. What variables in the raw data is `output` *motion_energy* derived from?\n\ni. A separate file, `motionEnergy_<anm>_<date>.mat`, sitting beside the data structure. What processing is involved in computing `output` *motion_energy*?\n\ni. None beyond binning. The value is already a single number per frame — the paper computes it per pixel as the difference of the median over the next and previous five frames, then reduces each frame to its 99th percentile across pixels — so there is nothing to smooth, differentiate, or combine. The trace is averaged into the 5 ms bins and split at the session median.\n\nii.\n```python\n_discretize(energy, np.nanpercentile(energy, SPLIT_PCT))\n```\n\niii. The spatial reduction has already been done upstream, so re-deriving anything would only discard information.\n\n## 9-d. How is `output` *motion_energy* aligned with the neural data?\n\ni. Same offset and same grid as the tracking. Motion energy has exactly one value per frame of the side camera, so its frame times are that camera's, corrected by the session offset and the trial's go cue, then trimmed to the window and binned.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef motion_energy(self):\n    \"\"\"Binned motion energy, as (n_trials, N_BINS).\"\"\"\n    rows = []\n    for trial in self.trials:\n        time = self._frame_time(trial, SIDE)       # motion energy follows the side camera\n        inside = (time >= T_START) & (time <= T_STOP)\n        rows.append(_bin_frames(time[inside], self.energy[trial][inside]))\n    return np.array(rows)\n```\n\niii. Same as above, motion energy uses the camera frames time index.\n\n## 10. How are minor mistakes in the data, e.g. missing data, handled?\n\ni. Three cases, all handled by keeping the trial and marking the gap rather than by filling anything in. **Missing frame times:** three trials in the whole dataset have `frameTimes` entirely NaN, so no frame can be placed on the go-cue clock; `_velocity` returns early and those trials come out as 1000 `not visible` bins for the tongue and paw. **Untracked frames:** wherever DeepLabCut's likelihood is at or below 0.9 the coordinates are already NaN, and those bins get the `not visible` class. **Mismatched frame counts:** in one trial the two cameras recorded different numbers of frames, so each feature is timed by its own camera rather than by the side camera.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef _velocity(self, track):\n    \"\"\"Combined velocity over the valid frames, NaN elsewhere.\"\"\"\n    time, x, y, likelihood = track\n    speed = np.full(time.size, np.nan)\n    if time.size < 2:                              # a few trials have no frame times\n        return time, speed\n```\n\niii. Nothing is interpolated or nearest-filled, because a missing camera frame is genuinely missing information and inventing a velocity for it would put a fabricated class into the output. The `not visible` class exists exactly so those bins can be represented honestly; the format forbids NaN, so some code has to be assigned. Trials with missing video are kept rather than dropped, since their neural, behavioural, and motion-energy data are unaffected.\n\n## 11-a. What are the most time-consuming steps of the code?\n\ni. Reading the files. Loading each session dominates its runtime; everything computed afterwards — spike binning, velocities, discretisation — is cheap by comparison. The whole conversion runs in about 135 s.\n\nii.\n```python\ndef load_mat(path):\n    \"\"\"Load a data_structure .mat as nested dicts (files are either v7.3 HDF5 or v5).\"\"\"\n```\n\niii. The data has to be read once either way, so this is not reducible.\n\n## 11-b. What loops in the code could have been vectorized to improve efficiency?\n\ni. Three loops remain over trials — the per-trial velocity in `_trial_velocity`, and the binning inside `tongue_velocity`, `paw_velocity`, and `motion_energy` — plus one over clusters in `rates`. They stay as loops because each trial has a different number of camera frames, so there is no rectangular array to operate on. The one place a per-trial loop was avoidable is the spike counting, which is a single `histogram2d` over all trials at once.\n\nii.\n```python\ncounts, _, _ = np.histogram2d(spike_trial, spike_time, bins=[trial_edges, BIN_EDGES])\n```\n\niii. Each file is read once, the video offset is computed once per session in `Camera.__init__` rather than per trial, each feature's frame-resolution velocity is computed once and reused by the binning and by the percentile, and the bin grid is built once at module level and shared by every trial, session, and stream.\n\nii.\n```python\nself.offset = self._video_offset()             # one constant for the whole session\n...\nself.side_tongue = self._trial_velocity(SIDE_TONGUE)\nself.bottom_tongue = self._trial_velocity(BOTTOM_TONGUE)\nself.paw = self._trial_velocity(PAW)\n```\n\niii. The index keeps the original trial numbers, which\n# every later step uses to reach back into the raw arrays.\n\ndef trial_column(bp, *names):\n    \"\"\"One entry per trial from a field of bp, e.g. trial_column(bp, 'stim', 'enable').\"\"\"\n    n_trials = int(np.ravel(bp['Ntrials'])[0])\n    field = bp\n    for name in names:\n        field = field[name]\n    return np.ravel(np.asarray(field, float))[:n_trials]\n\n\ndef trial_info(bp):\n    \"\"\"Outcome, context, and lick direction per trial, without early-lick or photostim trials.\"\"\"\n    hit = trial_column(bp, 'hit') > 0\n    miss = trial_column(bp, 'miss') > 0\n    right = trial_column(bp, 'R') > 0\n    autowater = trial_column(bp, 'autowater') > 0\n    early = trial_column(bp, 'early') > 0\n    stim = trial_column(bp, 'stim', 'enable') > 0\n    n_trials = hit.size\n\n    # a hit is a correct lick and a miss an incorrect one; the animal ignored the rest\n    outcome = np.full(n_trials, OUTCOME['ignore'])\n    outcome[hit] = OUTCOME['correct']\n    outcome[miss] = OUTCOME['incorrect']\n\n    # water is given from a random port without any cue in the WC context\n    context = np.where(autowater, CONTEXT['WC'], CONTEXT['DR'])\n\n    # a hit licks the instructed port, a miss licks the other one, an ignore neither\n    lick_direction = np.full(n_trials, LICK['no lick'])\n    lick_direction[hit] = np.where(right[hit], LICK['right'], LICK['left'])\n    lick_direction[miss] = np.where(right[miss], LICK['left'], LICK['right'])\n\n    info = pd.DataFrame({'lick_direction': lick_direction, 'context': context,\n                         'outcome': outcome})\n    info.index.name = 'trial'\n    return info[~early & ~stim]\n\n\n# ------------------------------------------------------------------- camera --\n# Tongue velocity, paw velocity, and motion energy for one session. \"\"\"Mean of the valid frames in each bin, NaN where a bin holds no valid frame.\"\"\"\n    bin_of_frame = np.searchsorted(BIN_EDGES, time, side='right') - 1\n    valid = np.isfinite(values) & (bin_of_frame >= 0) & (bin_of_frame < N_BINS)\n    total = np.bincount(bin_of_frame[valid], weights=values[valid], minlength=N_BINS)\n    count = np.bincount(bin_of_frame[valid], minlength=N_BINS)\n 1), np.nan)\n\n\ndef _discretize(values, threshold):\n    \"\"\"Two classes split at the threshold; untracked bins take the trailing class.\"\"\"\n    code = np.where(values >= threshold, self._velocity(self._track(trial, feature)) for trial in self.trials}\n\n    def _video_offset(self):\n        \"\"\"Seconds by which the video clock leads the behavior clock & (time <= T_STOP)\n        return time[inside], x[inside], y[inside], likelihood[inside]\n\n    # smooth the x, y postion, and compute the speed, filter by the likelihood threshold > 0.90\n    def _velocity(self, track):\n        \"\"\"Combined velocity over the valid frames, NaN elsewhere.\"\"\"\n        time, x, y, likelihood = track\n        speed = np.full(time.size, np.nan)\n        if time.size < 2:                              # a few trials have no frame times\n            return time, speed\n\n        sigma = SMOOTH_SIGMA_MS / 1000 / np.median(np.diff(time))\n        valid = likelihood > LIKELIHOOD_CUT            # x and y are NaN below this\n\n        # smooth and differentiate inside each run of tracked frames, never across a gap\n        for start, stop in _runs(valid):\n            if stop - start < 2:                       # a lone frame has no velocity\n                continue\n            sx = gaussian_filter1d(x[start:stop], sigma, all reference analyses align neural, kinematic, and ME data to the go cue (in WC trials, the \"go cue\" time is the water drop time, stored in the same `bp.ev.goCue` field).\n- Window: tmin=-2.5 s, tmax=+2.5 s relative to the go cue.\n- Binning: `dt` = 5-30 ms depending on script (WorkingWithDataObjs 10 ms; Figure 3 scripts 30 ms; getDefaultParams 5 ms). Decoding analyses re-bin neural data to **75 ms**.\n- Smoothing: causal Gaussian kernel, `params.smooth = 15` bins, 'reflect' boundary.\n- Video/ephys sync: frameTimes must be shifted by `vidshift = mode(sglx.bitcode.bitstart)/fs - mode(bp.ev.bitStart)` (~0.49-0.5 s).\n\n### Curation Steps\n**Neuron curation rules**:\n1. Exclude clusters whose quality is garbage/noisy/'real?' (findClusters with quality='all').\n2. Exclude clusters with mean firing rate <= 1 spk/s (removeLowFRClusters, params.lowFR=1; paper: \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\").\n3. Use only the ALM probe(s) as listed in the reference meta scripts / `obj.ex.probe.loc`.\n\n**Trial curation rules**:\n- Analyses exclude `stim.enable` (photoinactivation) trials and `early` (early lick) trials; ignore trials excluded from most analyses but are a required decoder output class here, so they are retained (see Step 5).\n- Sessions with < 10 units excluded.\n\n### Decoders Trained (reference)\n| Decoded variable | Method | Accuracy |\n|---|---|---|\n| Choice (R vs L, correct trials) from neural population | logistic regression per 75-ms bin, ridge, 4-fold | ~0.5 (chance) before go cue rising to ~0.9-1.0 after go cue (Fig. 3b) |\n| Context (DR vs WC) from neural population | same | ~0.7-0.9 across the trial incl. ITI (Fig. 4b) |\n| Choice from CDchoice projections (delay epoch) | logistic regression + ROC | AUC ~0.8-0.9 (ED Fig. 2c) |\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Check for Consistency\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nCross-checks run (scripts in `/app/cache/`): `survey.py`, `unitcheck.py`, `variants*.py`, `lickcheck.py`, `videocheck.py`.\n\n### Discrepancies Found\n| Topic | Code says | Data shows | Paper says | Resolution |\n|-------|-----------|------------|------------|------------|\n| # fixed-delay ephys sessions | 25 uncommented entries in load*_ALMVideo.m | 25 `data_structure` files in `Ephys_Behavior` | \"25 sessions\" | consistent -> use all 25 |\n| # randomized-delay sessions | 19 uncommented entries (JEB23 2023-10-20 commented out; JEB24 10-03/10-04 absent) | 22 files (2 without any units, 1 duplicate-like 10-20) | \"19 sessions\" | use the 19 reference sessions |\n| # mice (fixed delay) | 10 animals in meta scripts; `NullPotent/SessionMeta.csv` has 24 sessions / 9 animals (no EKH1) | 10 animals have fixed-delay files | \"nine mice\" | The paper's 9 mice = SessionMeta.csv list. probe 2 there is L M1TJ per `obj.ex.probe.loc`, so for those sessions we keep **only the ALM probe** -> see Key Decisions).\n- `subjects` = the 14 animals; `subject_idx` per session.\n- `brain_regions` = ['ALM']; every included neuron is in ALM.\n\n### Variable Mapping\n| Source Variable | Target Field | Transform | Reference Code Function(s) | Notes |\n|-----------------|--------------|-----------|----------------------------|-------|\n| `obj.clu{alm}.trialtm`, `.trial` | `neural` | align to go cue (subtract `bp.ev.goCue`), bin -2.5..2.5 s at dt=30 ms, rate = count/dt, causal-Gaussian smooth (N=15, 'reflect') | alignSpikes.m, getSeq.m, mySmooth.m | firing rate in spikes/s, float32 |\n| time axis | `input[0]` = `time_from_gocue` | obj.time = bin centers, seconds | getSeq.m | continuous, time-varying (1 x T) |\n| first lick after go cue (`bp.ev.lickL/lickR`) | `output[0]` = `lick_direction` | 0=left, 1=right, 2=none | firstLickTime.m | per-trial value broadcast over T |\n| `bp.autowater` | `output[1]` = `context` | 0=WC (autowater=1), 1=DR | params.condition strings | per-trial |\n| `bp.hit/miss/no` | `output[2]` = `outcome` | 0=incorrect(miss), 1=correct(hit), 2=ignore(no) | getOutcome.m | per-trial |\n| side-cam `tongue` x/y (`obj.traj{1}`) | `output[3]` = `tongue_velocity` | speed=|d(x,y)/dt| of interpolated position; 0 if < session median, 1 if >= median, 2 if tongue not visible (DLC NaN) | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m | time-varying |\n| bottom-cam `top_paw`,`bottom_paw` (`obj.traj{2}`) | `output[4]` = `paw_velocity` | mean speed of the visible paw markers; 0/1 by session median, 2 if neither paw visible | findPosition.m, findVelocity.m | time-varying |\n| `motionEnergy_*.mat` `me.data` | `output[5]` = `motion_energy` | interp to trial time axis (frameTimes - vidshift - goCue), fillmissing nearest; 0/1 by session median, 2 if the trial has no usable video | loadMotionEnergy.m | time-varying |\n\n### Key Decisions\n1. **Alignment to go cue** (`params.alignEvent='goCue'`), window **-2.5 to +2.5 s**, exactly as in every reference analysis script. In WC trials `bp.ev.goCue` holds the water-drop time, so the alignment is meaningful in both contexts.\n2. **Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\n3. **Causal Gaussian smoothing, N=15 bins, 'reflect'** exactly as `mySmooth` — causal so no information from the future leaks backwards in time (important for a decoder).\n4. **Neuron curation**: quality not in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, empty} (findClusters, case-insensitive/trimmed to handle label case and typos) AND mean firing rate over the trial window > 1 Hz (removeLowFRClusters with `lowFR=1`, matching the paper's \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"). Sessions with < 10 units would be dropped (paper criterion); in practice all 44 pass.\n5. **Probe selection**: use exactly the probe(s) listed in the reference meta scripts (`load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m`). These are the probes the paper analysed. For each kept probe the recorded region is read from `obj.ex.probe.loc` ('R ALM'/'L ALM' -> ALM, 'M1TJ' -> tjM1); when `loc` is missing or 'DUMMY', ALM is assumed (all the loader scripts are named *_ALMVideo and the paper states all recordings analysed were ALM). Consequence: for JEB15 2022-07-26/27/28 the reference uses probes [1 2] where probe 2 is 'L M1TJ', and for JEB15 2022-07-29 the reference uses probe 2 ('L M1TJ'); those neurons are labelled tjM1 so that `brain_region_idx` is truthful, rather than dropping data the reference analysed.\n6. **Trial curation**: exclude photoinactivation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) and early-lick trials (`bp.early`), exactly as every reference condition string does ('~stim.enable&~early') and as stated in the methods (\"Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward ('early lick') were omitted from analyses\"). **Ignore trials are kept** because 'ignore' and 'none' are required output classes.\n7. **Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class** instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`. This is required by the decoder output specification, which asks for an explicit 'not visible' category.\n8. **Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\n9. **Session curation**: keep a session only if it has >= 10 curated units (paper criterion) and at least 2 usable trials. No session is dropped for probe-location reasons (see Decision 5).\n10. **Video/ephys synchronisation** uses `vidshift` from `findVideoOffset.m` for both DLC and motion energy, as in the reference.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] Number of sessions = 44 (25 fixed + 19 randomized), animals = 14.\n- [ ] Units after curation: randomized-delay total = 845 (matches paper exactly).\n- [ ] Every session has >= 10 units; neurons/session distribution similar to ED Fig 2a (13-130).\n- [ ] Trial counts: sum of kept trials ~= total trials - early - stim.\n- [ ] Lick direction from first lick agrees with hit/miss x R/L in >99% of trials.\n- [ ] Outcome fractions: hit ~70%, miss ~12%, ignore ~13% (from raw bp fields).\n- [ ] Context fraction WC ~10-20% of trials overall (sessions with two contexts: 12 of 25 fixed-delay).\n- [ ] Each discretized output has ~50/50 split between classes 0 and 1 among visible timepoints.\n- [ ] Spot check (Step 10): recompute neural rate, tongue speed, ME for specific trials directly from the raw .mat files with independent code and compare with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Time axis: bin centers from -2.485 to 2.485, dt exactly 0.03 s.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\n`/app/convert_data.py` is self-contained (no imports from `/app/cache`). Structure:\n- `Session` class: unified reader for MAT v7 (scipy) and v7.3 (h5py) `data_structure` files; `load_motion_energy` handles the three motion-energy file variants.\n- Ports of the reference MATLAB routines: `time_axis` (getSeq.m), `gausswin`/`causal_kernel`/`mysmooth` (mySmooth.m), `bin_spikes` (alignSpikes.m + getSeq.m), `interp_to_axis`/`_fill_nearest` (interp1 + fillmissing('nearest')), `speed_from_xy` (findVelocity.m).\n- `process_session`: trial curation, neural binning, unit curation, behavioural outputs, video outputs, per-session discretization.\n- `plot_processing`: 14-panel figure per session covering every processing step.\n- `main`: multiprocessing pool over sessions, assembly, session curation, metadata, pickling.\n\nEfficiency:\n- Spike binning vectorised with `np.histogram2d` over (trial, aligned time) per unit instead of a per-trial loop (the reference's double loop over units x trials).\n- Smoothing done with `scipy.signal.fftconvolve` over all trials at once.\n- Video frames binned with `np.bincount` instead of per-bin loops.\n- Sessions processed in parallel with a `multiprocessing.Pool` (default 8 workers; memory-bound because v7.3 files are 90-250 MB each).\n\nCode inefficiencies identified: per-trial DLC reads from HDF5 dominate runtime (each trial is a separate dataset reference).\nCode speedups added: vectorised histogram binning, FFT smoothing, bincount frame binning, multiprocessing over sessions.\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Sample Conversion and Validation\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n\nRan `python -u /app/convert_data.py /app/sample_data.pkl --sample --show-processing` (sessions JEB6_2021-04-18 and JEB11_2022-05-10) -> `/app/conversion_sample_out.txt`, then `train_decoder.py --verify-only` -> `/app/verification_sample_out.txt` (**valid, no errors, no warnings**).\n\n### Sample Statistics\n| Statistic | Value |\n|-----------|-------|\n| Sessions | 2 |\n| Neurons (total) | 92 (29 + 63) |\n| Trials (total) | 625 (302 + 323) |\n| Trials / session | 302, 323 (of 382, 365 raw; In WC trials `bp.ev.goCue` holds the water-drop time, so the alignment is meaningful in both contexts.\n2. **Bin size 30 ms** = `params.dt = (1/100)*3` used in the paper's Figure 3 analysis scripts (other scripts use 5-10 ms; the decoding analyses re-bin to 75 ms). 30 ms keeps ~167 bins/trial, enough temporal resolution for licking (~7 Hz) while keeping the dataset tractable (~2.3M timepoints).\n3. **Causal Gaussian smoothing, N=15 bins, 'reflect'** exactly as `mySmooth` — causal so no information from the future leaks backwards in time (important for a decoder).\n4. **Neuron curation**: quality not in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, real?, empty} (findClusters, case-insensitive/trimmed to handle label case and typos) AND mean firing rate over the trial window > 1 Hz (removeLowFRClusters with `lowFR=1`, matching the paper's \"units with firing rates exceeding 1 Hz\"). Sessions with < 10 units would be dropped (paper criterion); in practice all 44 pass.\n5. **Probe selection**: use exactly the probe(s) listed in the reference meta scripts (`load<ANM>_ALMVideo.m`). These are the probes the paper analysed. For each kept probe the recorded region is read from `obj.ex.probe.loc` ('R ALM'/'L ALM' -> ALM, 'M1TJ' -> tjM1); when `loc` is missing or 'DUMMY', ALM is assumed (all the loader scripts are named *_ALMVideo and the paper states all recordings analysed were ALM). Consequence: for JEB15 2022-07-26/27/28 the reference uses probes [1 2] where probe 2 is 'L M1TJ', and for JEB15 2022-07-29 the reference uses probe 2 ('L M1TJ'); those neurons are labelled tjM1 so that `brain_region_idx` is truthful, rather than dropping data the reference analysed.\n6. **Trial curation**: exclude photoinactivation trials (`bp.stim.enable`) and early-lick trials (`bp.early`), exactly as every reference condition string does ('~stim.enable&~early') and as stated in the methods (\"Trials in which the animal contacted the lickport before the reward ('early lick') were omitted from analyses\"). **Ignore trials are kept** because 'ignore' and 'none' are required output classes.\n7. **Kinematics NaNs are kept as the 'not visible' class** instead of being filled/zeroed as in `findPosition`/`findVelocity`. This is required by the decoder output specification, which asks for an explicit 'not visible' category.\n8. **Discretization thresholds are per session** (median over all included trials and timepoints where the feature is visible), as specified in the decoder task.\n9. **Session curation**: keep a session only if it has >= 10 curated units (paper criterion) and at least 2 usable trials. No session is dropped for probe-location reasons (see Decision 5).\n10. **Video/ephys synchronisation** uses `vidshift` from `findVideoOffset.m` for both DLC and motion energy, as in the reference.\n\n### Planned Sanity Checks\n- [ ] Number of sessions = 44 (25 fixed + 19 randomized), animals = 14.\n- [ ] Units after curation: randomized-delay total = 845 (matches paper exactly).\n- [ ] Every session has >= 10 units; neurons/session distribution similar to ED Fig 2a (13-130).\n- [ ] Trial counts: sum of kept trials ~= total trials - early - stim.\n- [ ] Lick direction from first lick agrees with hit/miss x R/L in >99% of trials.\n- [ ] Outcome fractions: hit ~70%, miss ~12%, ignore ~13% (from raw bp fields).\n- [ ] Context fraction WC ~10-20% of trials overall (sessions with two contexts: 12 of 25 fixed-delay).\n- [ ] Each discretized output has ~50/50 split between classes 0 and 1 among visible timepoints.\n- [ ] Spot check (Step 10): recompute neural rate, tongue speed, ME for specific trials directly from the raw .mat files with independent code and compare with `np.allclose`.\n- [ ] Time axis: bin centers from -2.485 to 2.485, dt exactly 0.03 s.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Script Development\n**Status**: COMPLETE\n29:| findClusters | DataLoadingScripts/findClusters.m | CURATION | quality={'all'} -> keep all clusters EXCEPT quality in {garbage, gabrga, noisy, 'real?'} |\n32:| mySmooth | utils/mySmooth.m | PROCESSING | causal gaussian (gausswin(N), first half zeroed, normalized), 'reflect' boundary |\n35:| getKinematics | funcs/kinematics/getKinematics.m | PROCESSING | builds kin.dat (time,trials,feat): per DLC feature xdisp,ydisp,xvel,yvel + tongue_angle, tongue_length + motion_energy;
